title: Potential PrintNightmare Exploitation Attempt
rules_yaml:
title: Detects PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675) Prerequisite Registry Modifications
id: a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the modification of registry keys required to enable the PrintNightmare vulnerability. 
  Attackers disable restrictions on driver installation and anonymous access to SMB/RPC pipes to exploit CVE-2021-1675.
  This rule targets the preconditions for the attack rather than the exploitation itself, which is covered by other rules.
references:
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/012/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1547.012
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_pointandprint:
        TargetObject|contains: 'PointAndPrint'
        Details|contains:
            - 'RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators'
            - 'NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall'
    selection_smb_access:
        TargetObject|contains: 'NullSessionPipes'
        Details|contains: 'srvsvc'
    selection_anonymous:
        TargetObject|contains: 'RestrictAnonymous'
        Details|contains: '0x0'
    condition: selection_pointandprint or selection_smb_access or selection_anonymous
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate driver installation policy changes by administrators
    - System configuration hardening/relaxing scripts
level: high

title: Detects PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675) Exploitation via PointAndPrint DLL Load
id: b2c3d4e5-f6a7-8901-bcde-f12345678901
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the core exploitation phase of CVE-2021-1675. The Print Spooler service (spoolsv.exe) loads a malicious DLL 
  from a remote SMB share via the PointAndPrint mechanism. This rule monitors for unsigned or suspicious DLL loads 
  within the spoolsv.exe process, which is indicative of privilege escalation to SYSTEM.
references:
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/012/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1547.012
    - attack.t1021.002
logsource:
    category: image_load
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_spooler:
        Image|endswith: '\spoolsv.exe'
    selection_suspicious_dll:
        Signed: 'false'
        SignatureStatus: 'invalid' or 'not_signed'
    condition: selection_spooler and selection_suspicious_dll
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate printer driver updates (if unsigned drivers are used in the environment)
    - Known vendor-signed drivers with signature issues
level: high

title: Detects PrintNightmare (CVE-2021-1675) Exploit Script Execution
id: c3d4e5f6-a7b8-9012-cdef-123456789012
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects the execution of known exploit scripts used to leverage CVE-2021-1675. Specifically looks for 
  CVE-2021-1675.py being executed with command-line arguments pointing to a remote SMB share and target IP, 
  indicating an active exploitation attempt.
references:
    - https://github.com/cube0x0/CVE-2021-1675
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_exploit_script:
        Image|endswith: '\python.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'CVE-2021-1675.py'
    selection_smb_share:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '\\\\'
            - '.dll'
    condition: selection_exploit_script and selection_smb_share
falsepositives:
    - Security researchers testing vulnerability patches
    - Automated patch verification tools (if they use similar scripts)
level: high

attack_vector.entry_point: RPC endpoint MS-RPRN (Print System Remote Protocol) via named pipe or TCP port 445
attack_vector.attacker_controlled_input: Path to the malicious DLL in the PointAndPrint driver installation request

Configuration change to enable the vulnerability condition, often performed by defenders or attackers during setup, but distinct from the exploit execution itself; however, since it enables the specific vector, it's borderline. Given the prompt asks for 'not part of the attack itself' in terms of workflow vs exploit, this is a precondition setup. The PoC analysis lists it as setup. I will include it as incidental because it's configuration/preconditioning, not the exploitation trigger.

attack_vector.reasoning: The text explicitly details the CVE-2021-1675 (PrintNightmare) exploit which relies on the PointAndPrint feature to load a malicious DLL via SMB/RPC. The PoC code and configuration snippets clearly show the attacker-controlled input (DLL path) and the protocol (SMB/RPC).

pipeline.attack_summary: The attack leverages the PrintNightmare vulnerability (CVE-2021-1675) to achieve privilege escalation. An authenticated attacker with low privileges abuses the PointAndPrint driver installation mechanism via the MS-RPRN RPC endpoint to force the Print Spooler service (running as SYSTEM) to load a malicious DLL from a remote SMB share. This is facilitated by disabling security policies that restrict driver installation and allowing anonymous access to SMB shares.

ttp_mappings.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Print Processors
ttp_mappings.relevance: The exploit abuses the PointAndPrint feature to install a malicious print processor DLL that loads with SYSTEM privileges.
The attacker uses SMB to host the malicious DLL and connect to the target's RPC endpoints over port 445.
CVE-2021-1675 is a vulnerability allowing low-privilege users to escalate to SYSTEM by abusing the Print Spooler.

ttp_mappings.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: AppInit DLLs (or similar DLL load hijacking)
ttp_mappings.relevance: While technically Print Processors, the mechanism is analogous to DLL loading via registry keys for privilege escalation.

ttp_mappings.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
ttp_mappings.relevance: PowerShell commands (New-SmbShare, icacls, REG ADD) are used to configure the environment for the attack.

logsource_suggestions.reasoning: The attack requires modifying specific registry keys (NullSessionPipes, RestrictAnonymous, PointAndPrint policies) to enable the vulnerability. Detecting these changes is critical.
The exploit script (CVE-2021-1675.py) and supporting tools (rpcdump.py) are executed via command line. Additionally, the spoolsv.exe process will load the malicious DLL.
The core of the exploit is the loading of a malicious DLL by the spoolsv.exe process. Detecting unsigned or suspicious DLL loads in system processes is key.
The target machine initiates an SMB connection to the attacker's share to download the malicious DLL.
Windows Security logs capture RPC activity and authentication events related to the SMB/RPC connection and the spooler service interactions.

title: Lace Tempest PowerShell Evidence Eraser
rules_yaml:
title: Detects SysAid Path Traversal WebShell Upload via HTTP POST
id: 33c618ed-8604-49ec-8db7-21f0c16c3d01
status: experimental
description: Detects the upload of a malicious WAR archive to the SysAid Tomcat webroot via path traversal. This corresponds to the initial access vector where an attacker exploits CVE-2023-47246 to deploy a WebShell.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
    - attack.t1505.003
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_upload:
        cs-method: 'POST'
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - '.war'
            - 'usersfiles'
    condition: selection_upload
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate application updates or deployments
    - Automated backup processes uploading WAR files
level: high

title: Detects GraceWire Loader Execution via PowerShell and user.exe
id: d67836b2-a075-4194-8e84-577d11b1d68f
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of the GraceWire trojan loader (user.exe) launched via a hidden PowerShell process. This indicates successful exploitation and initial code execution on the host.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1620/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.defense-evasion
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1620
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_powershell_suspicious:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-nop'
            - '-w hidden'
            - 'IEX'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - '179.60.150.34'
    selection_userexe_hash:
        Image|endswith: '\user.exe'
        Hashes|contains:
            - 'b5acf14cdac40be590318dee95425d0746e85b1b7b1cbd14da66f21f2522bf4d'
    selection_userexe_parent:
        Image|endswith: '\user.exe'
        ParentImage|contains: '\SysAidServer\tomcat\webapps\'
    condition: (selection_powershell_suspicious) or (selection_userexe_hash) or (selection_userexe_parent)
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate PowerShell administration scripts
    - Automated deployment tools using PowerShell
level: high

title: Detects GraceWire Process Injection into System Processes
id: c5aa494a-2c13-4467-a09c-194a2db61bcb
status: experimental
description: Detects process injection attempts targeting critical Windows system processes, a technique used by the GraceWire trojan to hide its activity.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1055/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.defense-evasion
    - attack.t1055.001
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_target:
        TargetImage|endswith:
            - '\spoolsv.exe'
            - '\msiexec.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
    selection_access:
        GrantedAccess|contains:
            - '0x1F0FFF'
            - '0x1410'
            - '0x12a8'
    condition: selection_target and selection_access
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate system administration tools
    - Antivirus or EDR agents performing memory analysis
level: high

title: Detects Cobalt Strike C2 Communication via HTTP Download
id: 5d8eca24-c42b-495f-8f88-cf63009f3bfd
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound communication to the identified Cobalt Strike Command and Control server, indicating active remote access.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
    - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_c2_ip:
        dest_ip|contains:
            - '179.60.150.34'
            - '81.19.138.52'
            - '45.182.189.100'
    selection_c2_uri:
        cs-uri-query|startswith: '/a'
    condition: selection_c2_ip and selection_c2_uri
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software updates from known vendors
    - Cloud service API calls to similar IP ranges
level: high

title: Detects Log Cleaning and Artifact Deletion for Defense Evasion
id: 996da345-9b30-4ae5-90c6-3cab3e6b0ce4
status: experimental
description: Detects the deletion of malicious files and modification of log files to remove evidence of the attack, a common post-exploitation technique.
references:
    - https://www.sysaid.com/blog/service-desk/on-premise-software-security-vulnerability-notification
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/004/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1070/006/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-16
tags:
    - attack.defense-evasion
    - attack.t1070.004
    - attack.t1070.006
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_deletion_malware:
        EventType: 'FileDelete'
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\SysAidServer\tomcat\webapps\usersfiles.war'
            - '\SysAidServer\tomcat\webapps\usersfiles\user.exe'
    selection_log_modification:
        EventType|in:
            - 'FileDelete'
            - 'FileCreate'
            - 'FileModify'
        TargetFilename|contains: '\root\WEB-INF\logs\'
    condition: selection_deletion_malware or selection_log_modification
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate application uninstallation or cleanup scripts
    - Automated log rotation and archival tools
level: medium
